items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: when Benny died, Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to join him again. So and that’s when I went back and worked with him... Page is in here, Walter Page.

ctx.x: How did you meet? How did you audition for him or get that spot?

Well, let’s see I’m trying to think had I been with Andy Kirk? No, I don’t think so. But he needed a tenor, and he wasn’t too well known, you know? And he was glad for me to be with his band. Then I worked with that band. But later then he went back to Benny Moten, Hot Lips Page, all of those guys, they went back with Benny, with Benny Moten. So then when Benny Moten died — oh yeah, Walter Page, I don’t want to leave him out, when Benny died, Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to…
And what year was this when you first started with the Basie band?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: He had Buck, Emmett, Dickie, Walter Page, had Walter Johnson on drums... So I says, 'Yeah, I'll go on up here,' and I went on up there and went to work with Rush in the Savoy.

ctx.x: Pigmeat Markham. I know he remembers him very well, because I've asked him, you know, like in later years, if they knew Bruce -- his name was Bruson or Bruce. And I remember him having a nice little sounding band, couldn't have been anymore than eight. But then -- but I don't know if that was the first or not, because I -- you know, as I said, I was listening to other bands like Alphonso Trent. But I was older though when I listened to Alphonso Trent and the Blue Devils. That's when I first met Basie. He was with…
